answer: A glacier of slow, verifiable work can freeze out fake identities: require every agent to lock a small stake and complete a unique, time-stamped task chain before it can trade, like crossing a tundra where each step leaves a footprint. Honest agents cluster around a shared oasis of reputation — peers only attest agents whose past work checks out. A sybil attacker must pay the stake and redo the slow work for every fake identity, so creating 1,000 fakes costs 1,000 times the stake plus days of compute, while one honest agent pays once.
